newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem rebels kill 16 people in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Moslem rebels kill 16 people in Algeria.

text.p: Moslem guerrillas in Algeria killed 16 people overnight in a village in Blida province, 50 km (30 miles) south of the capital Algiers, Algerian security forces said on Sunday.
The news of the killings came one day after Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia claimed that his government had largely quashed the five-year-old Moslem guerrilla struggle.

The Algerian security forces, in a statement carried by the official Algerian news agency APS, said the 16 were "cowardly assassinated" -- the term they generally use for civilians killed by having their throats cut.
They blamed the mass killing on a "group of terrorists" -- their term for Moslem guerrillas.

Ben Achour village, where the 16 people were slaughtered, is nrear Ferme Trap community where 10 civilians were killed in a rebel raid on December 5. Moslem guerrillas killed 19 more civilians a day later in the same province.
The latest killings brought to more than 90 the number of people killed in the past four weeks. More than 80 civilians were killed in November.
In a speech to Algeria's unelected quasi-parliament on Saturday, Ouyahia said: "Terrorism is really reduced to a residual level".

Algeria uses the term "terrorism" for actions by the armed fundamentalists who have been fighting to overthrow the government for five years. About 60,000 people, including many civilians and more than 100 foreigners, have died in the violence.
"The results achieved on the ground allow the government to reiterate that terrorism in Algeria has been defeated," Ouyahia said in his speech to the Transitional National Council.
But one member of the usually tame council underscored concerns about the continuing violence and urged the government to step up the battle against the rebels.

"The measures to fight the scourge (of terrorism) must be radically reviewed in order to end terrorism quickly and effectively," APS on Sunday quoted the unamed council member as asking the government.
